registration: Before R2 guard execution and new R2 business reproductions; R1 remains unchanged and unqualified for complete executable source closure
source_scope: Separate qualified checkout, new v2 service schema. Guard fixtures use disposable copied public source and disposable simulation accounts; no R1 account, balance, private key or running state is inspected or changed.
checks: All imported production060 helpers and package initializers are bound to current v2 financial identity
Changed/missing helper bytes, changed canonical approval and prepared-output mutation fail closed with warm prefix
Incremental and independent full public replay agree on each accepted fixture state
Historical action bytes, config and derived-summary mutation are rejected even with warm cached prefix
Source/approval/output error invalidates cached acceptance, then restored genuine fixture can independently requalify
Stale owner lease cannot exercise cached authority; concurrent writer denied and reopen does not inherit live cache
Unsupported original v1 schema is refused, never silently migrated into v2
Public final audit does not use the private cache
Fresh-process trace of actual native operation has every loaded repository module in financial source closure
Standard release source inventory contains current v2 files and all bound helpers/artifacts
limits: A finite software guard suite is not hostile-host security, historical R1 migration, a new financial grant, physical validation or commercial success. No acceptance based on mtimes, action count alone or producer-supplied digests is allowed.
stopping: One exact source-matched suite; retain failures with their original source. Repairs are prospective under explicit new source identity, not silent alteration of existing R1 or R2 business accounts.
